title: Endogenous Preferences as Vulnerability Signals: Discovering Universal Adversarial Triggers for LLM Utility Degradation
abstract: arXiv:2611.18592v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deployed large language models must remain useful when untrusted text enters their prompt context. Adversarial prompting and red-teaming methods typically define the failures they seek through task labels, harmful targets, judge feedback, or downstream utility scores. We ask whether a frozen model's clean behavior can reveal a reusable context vulnerability when its task-level form is unknown, and downstream task feedback is withheld. To study this question, EndoUT uses a Siamese-style design that compares the same frozen victim on clean and span-modified versions of each unlabeled instruction. Without a task-level target, the clean pass supplies the victim's preferred response-onset token as an instruction-conditioned reference; Endogenous Preference Disruption (EPD) measures how insertion weakens that preference. translated_title: 内源性偏好作为脆弱性信号：发现导致大语言模型效用退化的通用对抗触发器
translated_abstract: 部署的大语言模型在不可信文本进入其提示上下文时必须保持可用。对抗提示与红队测试方法通常通过任务标签、有害目标、评判者反馈或下游效用分数来定义其试图寻找的失败。我们探究：当任务级形式未知且下游任务反馈不可获取时，一个冻结模型的干净行为能否揭示可复用的上下文脆弱性。为研究这一问题，EndoUT采用孪生式设计，在每条无标签指令的干净版本与片段修改版本上比较同一冻结受害模型。在没有任务级目标的情况下，干净前向传递提供受害模型所偏好的响应起始token，作为指令条件化的参考；内源性偏好破坏（EPD）衡量片段插入在多大程度上削弱了这种偏好。一个辅助生成器提供有界片段提议；EPD引导其更新并在无法访问下游信息的情况下对候选池进行排序。
tldr: 该论文提出EndoUT方法，以冻结模型自身干净行为中的内源性偏好破坏（EPD）作为脆弱性信号，在无需任务标签或下游反馈的情况下自动发现可复用的通用对抗触发器，从而降低大语言模型的效用。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes EndoUT, which leverages endogenous preference disruption (EPD) from a frozen model's clean behavior as vulnerability signals to discover reusable universal adversarial triggers that degrade LLM utility without requiring task labels or downstream feedback.
